data.title: The TSC-mTOR signaling pathway regulates the innate inflammatory response
data.authors: Weichhart T; Costantino G; Poglitsch M; Rosner M; Zeyda M; Stuhlmeier KM; Kolbe T; Stulnig TM; Hörl WH; Hengstschläger M; Müller M; Säemann MD

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: The TSC-mTOR pathway controls the innate inflammatory response of monocytes/macrophages.
data.abstract_excerpt: The innate inflammatory immune response must be tightly controlled to avoid damage to the host. Here, we showed that the tuberous sclerosis complex-mammalian target of rapamycin (TSC-mTOR) pathway regulated inflammatory responses after bacterial stimulation in monocytes, macrophages, and primary dendritic cells. Inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin promoted production of proinflammatory cytokines via the transcription factor NF-kappaB but blocked the release of interleukin-10 via the transcription factor STAT3.

extracted_findings.effect: mTOR inhibition promotes pro-inflammatory cytokines via NF-κB – TSC-mTOR regulates the innate inflammatory response
